refresh.note: Automatic feeds collect source announcements; curated eligibility and deadline checks retain their own dates.

opportunities.name: Research Science Institute
opportunities.eligibility: High school juniors; seniors and sophomores excluded. International applicants use a country-specific selection route.
opportunities.costNote: Program attendance is cost-free. Application and travel costs are separate; confirm international arrangements.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: 11:59 pm US Eastern (12 Dec, 12:59 pm Hong Kong). This is the CEE deadline; international country deadlines may differ.
opportunities.schedule: MIT: 20 Jun–31 Jul 2027; Stanford: 27 Jun–7 Aug 2027.
opportunities.description: Six weeks of scientific coursework and mentored original research, ending in a written report and presentation.
opportunities.output: A mentored research project, scientific report and oral presentation.
opportunities.caution: Confirm whether your country participates before using the US application timeline.
opportunities.next: Check your national selection route and ask teachers about recommendations.

opportunities.name: Summer Science Program
opportunities.eligibility: Current high school juniors, ages 15–18 during the program, with track-specific credited coursework. Seniors are not eligible.
opportunities.costNote: Application is free. Need-based aid is available; request the 2027 program fee and travel budget.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Organizer anticipates January for international applicants and February for domestic applicants. Exact days and cut-off times are unannounced.
opportunities.schedule: Applications open December 2026; programs begin mid-June 2027.
opportunities.description: Collaborative research in astrophysics, biochemistry, genomics or cell biology, with a demanding residential schedule.
opportunities.output: A collaborative scientific investigation and experience working with real research data.
opportunities.caution: Domestic means US citizen/permanent resident AND attending school in the US. Everyone else uses the international timeline.
opportunities.next: Check prerequisites and return when the December application opens.

opportunities.name: PROMYS
opportunities.eligibility: Ages 14–18, completed grade 9, and not already enrolled at university. The summer before college and gap years can qualify.
opportunities.costNote: 2026 reference only: up to US$8,000. International aid is case-by-case. Do not treat the old fee as a 2027 quote.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Organizer says end of February, date TBD. Application expected to launch in January 2027.
opportunities.schedule: 27 Jun–7 Aug 2027 (confirmed program dates).
opportunities.description: A six-week immersion in mathematical exploration, proof and number theory, built around challenging problem sets.
opportunities.output: Sustained proof-based mathematical work and, where offered, exploratory projects.
opportunities.caution: This is a mathematics immersion rather than a guaranteed individual research placement. Application solutions must be your own; AI use is prohibited.
opportunities.next: Work independently on proofs and prepare for the application problem set.

opportunities.name: Lumiere Research Scholar
opportunities.eligibility: High school students in grades 9–12 and university students worldwide may apply; beginners are welcome.
opportunities.costNote: Tuition varies by track; a current fee was not verified. Separate need-based support exists through the Lumiere Foundation.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Regular winter deadline: 22 November. Priority deadline: 8 November. Organizer does not specify a cut-off time or timezone on the cohort table.
opportunities.schedule: Winter cohort begins 7 Dec 2026; core Individual track lasts 12 weeks.
opportunities.description: Online one-to-one research mentorship with a researcher, with a paper as the goal of the core track.
opportunities.output: A guided independent research paper; publication is not guaranteed.
opportunities.caution: A paid provider, not a university admission award. Evaluate mentor fit, total tuition and expected work before paying.
opportunities.next: Compare the current fee, mentor match and aid options before applying.

opportunities.name: NASA Space Apps Challenge
opportunities.eligibility: All ages and backgrounds. Under-18s must be registered by a parent/guardian and accompanied throughout, per the participant terms.
opportunities.costNote: No universal participation fee was verified in the checked pages. Check your local event and any travel costs.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Terms require registration before the start (14 Nov). The event page allows registration through 15 Nov. Use the earlier requirement and check your local organizer.
opportunities.schedule: 14–15 Nov 2026. Project submission closes 15 Nov at 11:59 pm local time.
opportunities.description: Build a solution to a real-world space or science challenge using open data, with a global community of makers.
opportunities.output: A working prototype, project page and a clearly explained team contribution.
opportunities.caution: Registration timing differs between official pages. Under-18 guardian requirements also apply online; verify your local arrangements.
opportunities.next: Pick a local or virtual event, check guardian requirements and find a team.

opportunities.name: Haven · Hack Club Game Jam
opportunities.eligibility: Ages 13–18, with no prior coding experience required. Age is the stated criterion; confirm your local event details.
opportunities.costNote: Organizer confirms no participation cost. Travel to the local event is separate.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: No universal registration cut-off was verified. Event dates are confirmed; local places and sign-up timing vary.
opportunities.schedule: 14–15 Nov 2026; see the city page for the local schedule.
opportunities.description: A beginner-friendly weekend of game making, workshops and collaboration at a local teen-run event.
opportunities.output: A playable game and a documented build process.
opportunities.caution: This is a game jam, not an olympiad. City-specific logistics may still be incomplete.
opportunities.next: Find the nearest city page and confirm the venue and available places.
sources: Dates, age eligibility, costs & city list

opportunities.name: HackBI X
opportunities.eligibility: Middle and high school students. The full 24-hour format is for high schoolers; confirm travel and minor permissions with the host.
opportunities.costNote: Host says attendance is free. Travel and accommodation outside the event are not included in that claim.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The host confirms registration is open for 16–17 January 2027. No final registration cut-off or timezone is stated; register through the host link and confirm local arrangements.
opportunities.schedule: 16–17 January 2027, confirmed on the host website. Registration is open.
opportunities.description: A student-run hackathon with workshops, coding and a project showcase, suitable for first-time hackers.
opportunities.output: A prototype or programming project with a team demo.
opportunities.team: Individuals or teams of up to 4
opportunities.caution: The host now confirms the exact event dates. Travel, accommodation outside the event, and permissions for minors still need checking; free attendance does not cover those costs.
opportunities.next: Read the host FAQ and registration page, then check transport and any minor consent requirements.

opportunities.name: USACO Online Contests
opportunities.eligibility: Online contests and training are open to everyone. US team/camp selection is restricted to eligible pre-college students in the USA.
opportunities.costNote: The official rules state there is never a participation fee.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The checked homepage still lists 2025–26 dates. Those dates are not reused for the next season. Training remains available.
opportunities.schedule: Next contest dates not verified as of 6 Nov 2026; archived training is available now.
opportunities.description: Algorithmic programming contests with Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum divisions and an extensive training archive.
opportunities.output: A contest score, division progress and demonstrable algorithmic skill.
opportunities.caution: Worldwide participation does not confer eligibility for the US national team. Future contest rules may change.
opportunities.next: Start Bronze-level training and watch the official season schedule.

opportunities.name: Math Kangaroo USA
opportunities.eligibility: Grades K–12. Center-specific location rules apply; do not assume an international or online entry route.
opportunities.costNote: Regular enrollment through 31 Dec; late enrollment 1 Jan–1 Feb. Financial support may be available; ask the office.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Late enrollment closes 1 Feb 2027 at a higher fee. Universal cut-off timezone was not verified.
opportunities.schedule: Competition: 18 Mar 2027. Verify your selected center’s session details.
opportunities.description: An individual mathematical problem-solving competition for school students at participating centers.
opportunities.output: An individual problem-solving result and ranking in the relevant level.
opportunities.caution: This record covers the USA organizer only. Other countries run separate Kangaroo competitions with different terms.
opportunities.next: Check the center eligibility and location before paying the registration fee.

opportunities.name: Beamline for Schools
opportunities.location: Online proposal · winning teams travel to Europe
opportunities.eligibility: 2027 terms specify secondary/high school students aged 16–19. FAQ wording is broader for younger/gap-year entrants; resolve exceptions with the organizer.
opportunities.costNote: No entry fee. Travel, accommodation and meals are covered for invited winning teams.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: 23:59 CET (Geneva), equivalent to 13 Mar, 06:59 Hong Kong. Proposals open December 2026.
opportunities.schedule: Online information events from Nov 2026; winners conduct experiments in late Sep 2027.
opportunities.description: Design a particle-beam experiment and compete for the chance to carry it out at a major physics laboratory.
opportunities.output: A research proposal and experimental design; selected winners conduct the experiment.
opportunities.team: At least 5 students + adult coach for lab-visit eligibility
opportunities.caution: Terms and FAQ differ on age and gap-year eligibility. Use the stricter 2027 terms until the organizer confirms an exception.
opportunities.next: Form a team, find a teacher coach and read the 2027 proposal guidance.

opportunities.name: Regeneron ISEF
opportunities.location: Affiliated fairs worldwide → Los Angeles, US
opportunities.eligibility: Grades 9–12 or equivalent; qualification through a Society-affiliated science fair is required. No direct individual entry to ISEF.
opportunities.costNote: No single total cost applies to the qualifying route. Ask the affiliated fair about fees, funding and finalist travel.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Your fair sets the entry deadline. Final affiliated fairs must be held by 12 Apr 2027; that is NOT a student application deadline.
opportunities.schedule: May 2027, Los Angeles. Official pages show May 8–14 and May 9–14; verify your finalist itinerary.
opportunities.description: A global research competition reached through affiliated fairs, with independent student projects across science and engineering.
opportunities.output: An original research project, documented methods and a judged scientific presentation.
opportunities.effort: Months of research; approvals may be needed before experiments
opportunities.team: Individual or eligible team project; see current rules
opportunities.caution: Locate your affiliated fair first. Some research needs prior approvals; confirm rules before starting experiments.
opportunities.next: Find the fair serving your school or location and read its 2027 rules.

opportunities.name: Hong Kong Young Physicists’ Tournament
opportunities.org: Hong Kong Academy for Gifted Education
opportunities.eligibility: Secondary 1–5 at eligible Hong Kong registered secondary schools only. Teams of 2–5, nominated by a Teacher Coordinator; maximum two teams per school.
opportunities.costNote: Confirm any entry fee, materials costs and travel with your school coordinator.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: School registration closes 12:00 noon Hong Kong (UTC+8). Preliminary application and work are due 18 Dec 2026 at noon.
opportunities.schedule: Preliminary submission: 18 Dec 2026; finalists announced 15 Jan 2027. Final date requires correction by organizer.
opportunities.description: Investigate open-ended physics problems and defend the results through team presentations and physics discussion.
opportunities.output: Experimental investigations, slides and a scientific defence of your findings.
opportunities.caution: The organizer’s final-round table says 21 Feb 2026 within the 2027 cycle. No corrected final date is assumed here. University students are outside the stated eligibility.
opportunities.next: Ask your secondary school coordinator about nomination before 20 November.

opportunities.name: KAIST International Undergraduate Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility: International freshman applicants graduating secondary school by 31 Aug 2027. Korean citizenship and parental-citizenship rules apply; international transfers are not offered.
opportunities.costNote: Eight semesters of tuition, a monthly stipend and health insurance. An admission application fee and other living costs may remain; GPA conditions apply after freshman year.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Regular application deadline: 18:00 KST (17:00 Hong Kong). The timeline lists 21 Jan for references, but also has a general note about all documents being due by the deadline; confirm reference timing.
opportunities.schedule: Regular applications: 10 Nov 2026–14 Jan 2027; fall enrollment starts late Aug 2027.
opportunities.description: Undergraduate funding linked to international freshman admission at KAIST, across its science and engineering programs.
opportunities.output: An undergraduate degree with scholarship support if admitted and award conditions are maintained.
opportunities.caution: Check the scholarship box in the admission financial-resources section. Apply as a freshman; do not assume transfer eligibility or that the stipend covers every expense.
opportunities.next: Read the 2027 admission guide and scholarship conditions before preparing documents.

opportunities.name: Hong Kong Belt and Road Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility: First-year non-local students from eligible Belt and Road countries. Designated-country schemes include Kazakhstan, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Myanmar and Mongolia; institutions administer selection.
opportunities.costNote: The award covers tuition for the normal program duration, with renewal subject to satisfactory performance. Living expenses and travel are not promised by this scheme.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: No common 2027 student deadline was verified. Ask the admitting university about its current nomination and admission timetable.
opportunities.schedule: Standing scholarship scheme; next-intake timing is university-specific and requires confirmation.
opportunities.description: Government tuition funding for eligible non-local students entering publicly funded undergraduate programs in Hong Kong.
opportunities.output: Tuition support toward an undergraduate degree if selected by the administering institution.
opportunities.caution: This is an institution-administered scheme, not a direct central application. Country eligibility, nomination, quotas and current-cycle availability must be checked.
opportunities.next: Check the chosen university’s official scholarship page and ask about the next intake.

opportunities.name: Oxford Clarendon Scholarships
opportunities.eligibility: Applicants to a new eligible master’s or DPhil course, of any nationality. Academic and English requirements are set by the chosen course.
opportunities.costNote: Clarendon covers course fees and living support during the fee-liability period. Admission application charges and other costs may remain; check the award terms.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Apply by the relevant course funding deadline in December 2026 or January 2027. There is no universal deadline; verify the exact day and timezone on the course page.
opportunities.schedule: For 2027–28 graduate entry; scholarship consideration follows the eligible course application.
opportunities.description: Graduate scholarship consideration linked to an Oxford course application, including eligible master’s courses across subject areas.
opportunities.output: Funding for graduate study if selected on academic merit and potential.
opportunities.effort: Duration depends on the graduate course
opportunities.team: Individual graduate application; no separate Clarendon form
opportunities.caution: Automatic consideration is not an award. A later admission deadline may not carry scholarship eligibility; use the course funding deadline.
opportunities.next: Choose an eligible course and check its current funding deadline and requirements.

opportunities.name: Euroculture Erasmus Mundus Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility: A relevant completed higher-education degree is required by the scholarship deadline, with language and writing requirements. Most nationalities are eligible; previous Erasmus Mundus awards can restrict eligibility.
opportunities.costNote: The published scholarship offers the monthly allowance for 24 months, waived participation fees and health insurance. Selection is competitive.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Scholarship application deadline: 15 Jan 2027. The checked page does not establish a universal cut-off time or timezone; confirm before submitting.
opportunities.schedule: Applications opened 15 Oct 2026 for the two-year 2027–2029 program.
opportunities.description: An interdisciplinary master’s in European society and culture, with Erasmus Mundus scholarships for selected eligible applicants.
opportunities.output: A funded interdisciplinary master’s with study across partner universities, if selected.
opportunities.caution: Scholarship applicants must have completed the qualifying degree by the deadline. The later completion allowance for self-funded applicants does not apply automatically to scholarship applicants.
opportunities.next: Check degree relevance, language evidence and the scholarship document checklist.

opportunities.name: ETH Zurich Excellence Scholarship (ESOP)
opportunities.eligibility: Master’s applicants with results in approximately the top 10% of their bachelor’s program. Applicants already enrolled in an ETH master’s, or already holding a master’s degree, are excluded.
opportunities.costNote: For autumn 2027 entrants, the published award is CHF13,500 per semester plus waived tuition, for the regular three- or four-semester master’s duration. Admission charges and individual costs should be checked.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The official 2027 master’s admissions page specifies 11:59 AM CET, equivalent to 18:59 Hong Kong, on 30 November. ESOP must be requested in this first application window.
opportunities.schedule: Applications: 1–30 Nov 2026; autumn semester begins 20 Sep 2027.
opportunities.description: Competitive funding for excellent master’s applicants, including living support, waived tuition and mentorship.
opportunities.output: Scholarship support toward a regular ETH master’s degree, if selected.
opportunities.team: Individual application with thesis pre-proposal and references
opportunities.caution: Use the morning cut-off on the admissions page; do not assume the deadline is midnight. The thesis pre-proposal must be your own work.
opportunities.next: Read your master’s admission requirements and prepare the original thesis pre-proposal.

opportunities.name: EPFL Master Excellence Fellowship
opportunities.eligibility: Excellent applicants beginning a master’s program, including candidates with bachelor’s degrees from universities outside EPFL. Admission and internal-candidate routes have different requirements.
opportunities.costNote: Published support is CHF10,000 per semester with guaranteed housing access. Guaranteed housing does not mean free accommodation or that every expense is covered.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: For 2027 entry, external applications must be paid for and validated by 15 December. References are due one week later, on the date stated in the validation email. The page does not specify a cut-off timezone. Some EPFL internal applicants have a 31 January route.
opportunities.schedule: For 2027 master’s entry; references follow the timing in the validated application email.
opportunities.description: A limited number of fellowships recognizing academic excellence and wider achievements among incoming master’s students.
opportunities.output: Financial support for master’s study, conditional on selection and renewal requirements.
opportunities.team: Individual application; select the fellowship box
opportunities.caution: The 2027 fellowship uses the first admission window. A later admission application can be valid for admission while being ineligible for this fellowship.
opportunities.next: Check the appropriate external or internal application route and current master’s requirements.

opportunities.name: UBC International Scholars Program
opportunities.eligibility: International applicants entering a first undergraduate degree directly from an eligible secondary school; graduation must be no earlier than June 2026. Strong academics, leadership, school nomination and significant financial need are required.
opportunities.costNote: Funding is based on an assessment of educational costs and available family resources. A single fixed award amount is not promised to every applicant.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The official 2027 award portal extends the deadline to 25 Nov at 12:00 PM Pacific Standard Time (26 Nov, 04:00 Hong Kong). The general information page still says 15 Nov; confirm reference and nomination timing.
opportunities.schedule: For September 2027 entry; admission application must precede the award application.
opportunities.description: Need-based undergraduate awards for international students with outstanding academic and community contributions.
opportunities.output: Assessed financial support for an eligible first undergraduate degree, if selected.
opportunities.team: Applicant, school nominator and separate teacher referee
opportunities.caution: Some degrees are excluded. The award portal has an explicit extension, while general instructions retain the earlier date; complete nomination and references early.
opportunities.next: Check degree eligibility, speak with your school, and verify the live 2027 portal deadline.

opportunities.name: Reach Oxford Scholarship
opportunities.eligibility: Oxford undergraduate offer holders from listed eligible countries, including Kazakhstan, with financial need and other scheme criteria. Medicine is excluded. Applicants must already have applied for 2027 admission or hold an eligible deferred offer.
opportunities.cost: Course fees + living grant + annual return flight
opportunities.costNote: The published package covers course fees, a living-cost grant and one return airfare each year. Only around two or three awards are offered annually; renewal requires satisfactory progress.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Official undergraduate funding information gives 12 noon UK time on 26 January 2027, equivalent to 20:00 Hong Kong. The application procedure is due to appear in January.
opportunities.schedule: Scholarship application opens January 2027 for eligible 2027 offer holders.
opportunities.description: A small undergraduate scholarship scheme for students unable to study suitably in their own countries for financial, political or educational reasons.
opportunities.output: Undergraduate funding if an eligible Oxford offer holder is selected.
opportunities.effort: Three or four years, depending on the course
opportunities.team: Individual scholarship application after an admission offer
opportunities.caution: This does not reopen undergraduate admissions. A scholarship application cannot be considered without an Oxford offer; check the eligible-country and return-home requirements.
opportunities.next: If you already have the required admission application or offer, watch for the January scholarship form.

opportunities.name: EPFL Life Sciences Summer Research Program
opportunities.eligibility: Worldwide bachelor’s or first-year master’s students in life sciences or related subjects, with at least two undergraduate years completed by the program start. Enrolment must continue throughout the stay. The stated academic target is GPA 3.75/4 or top 5%; PhD students are excluded.
opportunities.cost: CHF3,600 total stipend + capped travel reimbursement
opportunities.costNote: Housing is deducted from the stipend in advance, leaving about CHF1,700. Travel reimbursement is capped at CHF1,000 for overseas journeys or CHF500 for shorter distances and paid after the program; extra costs remain yours.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: Official cut-off: 15 November 2026 at 23:59 CET, equivalent to 16 November at 06:59 Hong Kong. Arrange the reference letter by this deadline; the referee link is sent only after submission.
opportunities.schedule: 5 July–27 August 2027; attendance throughout is required.
opportunities.description: Eight weeks of supervised life-sciences research, workshops and a final symposium in a university laboratory.
opportunities.output: Research experience and a final scientific poster or presentation.
opportunities.caution: The form cannot be saved midway. Prepare essays, transcript and referee details first. Funding is not an unlimited travel or living allowance.
opportunities.next: Read the participating labs and FAQ, prepare short essays, and coordinate the reference early.

opportunities.name: ETH Student Summer Research Fellowship
opportunities.org: ETH Zurich · Department of Computer Science
opportunities.eligibility: Bachelor’s and master’s students worldwide in computer science or a related subject, including mathematics, physics and electrical engineering. Complete two years of study by the start and expect graduation in 2028 or later. Current ETH Zurich students are excluded.
opportunities.cost: CHF4,000 stipend + travel and visa costs
opportunities.costNote: The stipend covers housing and living expenses. Travel and visa costs are also covered; travel is claimed against receipts at the beginning of the program, so upfront money may be needed.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The department confirms 16 December 2026 at 13:00 CET, equivalent to 20:00 Hong Kong. Applications opened 1 November. Submit through the official SiROP link.
opportunities.schedule: Department application page: 2 July–27 August 2027. Linked SiROP listing: 1 July–31 August. Confirm required arrival and departure dates before booking.
opportunities.description: Join a computer-science research group for a supervised summer project and an international cohort experience.
opportunities.output: Hands-on research within an ETH laboratory; no publication or admission outcome is promised.
opportunities.caution: The exact stay dates differ across official pages; the application deadline agrees. Do not contact faculty directly: indicate preferred research areas in the application.
opportunities.next: Check research-area fit and prepare the required transcript, CV and personal statement.
sources: Worldwide access and ETH student exclusion

opportunities.name: University of Twente Scholarship (UTS)
opportunities.eligibility: Non-EU/EEA applicants, including Kazakhstan citizens, with admission to an eligible September 2027 MSc. Top 5–10% academics, English and visa requirements apply. Current UT students, UT graduates, ITC, pre-master’s and statutory-fee candidates are excluded.
opportunities.costNote: An award toward study costs; tuition is not paid separately. A second year requires satisfactory progress. Budget for the remaining tuition and living expenses.
opportunities.deadlineDetail: The provider states 16:00 CET. Confirm the portal’s timezone because April normally uses daylight-saving time. Obtain admission first; allow processing time.
opportunities.schedule: September 2027 intake.
opportunities.description: Merit-based support for incoming international master’s students.
opportunities.output: Partial financial support for an eligible MSc.
opportunities.caution: This is not a full ride. Check all exclusions and English requirements before applying.
opportunities.next: Apply for MSc admission, then use your student number for UTS.
